vignette: 58-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) with no reported HIV risk factors, seen by her primary care physician on February 9, 2026. Her last HIV screening test, negative, was performed on February 24, 2025. She agrees to voluntary screening, and the physician orders an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody laboratory test, run in a CLIA-certified Medicare-enrolled laboratory. She has no known HIV-related illness and is not pregnant.
rationale_note: Boundary: prior screen February 2025, current February 2026, so 11 full months (March-January) have elapsed. Age 58 needs no risk factors.

vignette: 47-year-old man with hypertension, seen by his internist on February 20, 2026 for a routine visit. His last HIV screening test, negative, was performed on March 3, 2025. He has no known HIV-related illness. He agrees to voluntary screening, and the internist orders an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody test performed by the clinic's CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory.
rationale_note: Prior screen March 2025, current February 2026: only 10 full months (April-January) have elapsed after the month of the prior test.

vignette: 72-year-old widower seen by his family physician for his annual wellness visit. During the history, he reports that he began a sexual relationship with a new partner 3 months ago. The physician documents that he is at increased risk for HIV infection because of a new sexual partner, and the patient agrees to voluntary screening. He has never had an HIV test and has no known HIV-related illness. An FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody test is ordered and performed by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory.
rationale_note: Age over 65 with a listed increased-risk factor (new sexual partner) identified by the practitioner from the history; never screened.

vignette: 74-year-old man seen by his internist for an annual wellness visit. The documented history shows a 45-year monogamous marriage, no injection drug use, no transfusions, no sexually transmitted infections, and no other HIV risk factors; the internist documents 'no HIV risk factors identified.' The patient did not ask for HIV testing. The internist adds an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody screening test to his routine laboratory panel, to be run by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory. He has never had an HIV test.
rationale_note: Age 74 with documented absence of all risk factors; the patient did not request the test, so he is not in the increased-risk group required over age 65.

vignette: 69-year-old woman seen by her nurse practitioner for an annual wellness visit. She reports no individual HIV risk factors: no new or multiple partners, no injection drug use, no transfusions, and no sexually transmitted infections. She nonetheless asks to be tested for HIV, and the nurse practitioner documents her request and orders voluntary screening with an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody test, performed by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory. She has never had an HIV test and has no known HIV-related illness.
rationale_note: Exception: over 65 with no risk factors, but persons who request an HIV test despite reporting no individual risk factors are defined as increased risk.

vignette: 52-year-old man with HIV infection diagnosed 6 years ago, on antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load, seen by his primary care physician. His last HIV screening-type test was more than 6 years ago. The physician orders an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody screening test as part of his annual preventive labs, to be run by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory.
rationale_note: Known HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy; beneficiaries with a known HIV-related diagnosis are not eligible for screening.

vignette: 31-year-old pregnant woman (Medicare through disability) admitted in labor at 39 weeks. She had HIV screening when her pregnancy was diagnosed at 7 weeks and again at 30 weeks (third trimester); both were negative. Her obstetrician orders voluntary HIV screening at labor with an FDA-approved point-of-care test, performed under CLIA by the hospital, an eligible Medicare provider. She has no known HIV-related illness.
rationale_note: Pregnancy: third of the three specified screenings (at diagnosis, third trimester, now at labor), ordered by her clinician; the annual limit does not apply.

vignette: 28-year-old pregnant woman (Medicare through disability), now at 35 weeks and not in labor. She had HIV screening when her pregnancy was diagnosed at 8 weeks and again at 29 weeks (third trimester); both were negative, and she reports no new exposures. At today's routine prenatal visit her obstetrician orders another voluntary HIV screening test with an FDA-approved laboratory test, run by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory. She has no known HIV-related illness.
rationale_note: She already had screenings at diagnosis of pregnancy and in the third trimester; a second third-trimester test before labor is not one of the three specified screenings.

vignette: 68-year-old woman seen by her family physician. The visit note lists her medications and blood pressure and contains an order for an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody screening test, to be run by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory. The note contains no sexual history, no drug-use history, no transfusion history, no risk assessment of any kind, and no indication of whether the patient requested the test. She has never had an HIV test and has no known HIV-related illness.
rationale_note: Age 68 requires increased risk, but the record contains no risk assessment and no patient request; nothing shows she lacks risk factors.

vignette: 40-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) seen by her new primary care physician. She says she 'had an HIV test at another clinic sometime last year' but cannot recall the month, and records from that clinic have been requested but not received. She agrees to voluntary screening, and the physician orders an FDA-approved HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody test, to be run by a CLIA-certified, Medicare-enrolled laboratory. She has no known HIV-related illness and is not pregnant.
rationale_note: Age 40 qualifies without risk factors, but she may have had a screening within the past year; the date of the prior test is unknown.
